title: Oscar and the Veil
premise: Theo Iversen, gatekeeper and ledger-keeper of the Veiled Guild, has spent his life trading in impossible things while keeping the old gate beneath his tower sealed. When a mute child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Theo discovers she is the last vessel of the Veil — the binding that holds a long-dead king's crown from waking. The Guild's masters intend to sell her to the thing already wearing the living king's face, and as winter deepens, the Veil thins across the realm. Theo, who has never broken a rule, must smuggle the child through the guild's own impossible markets, gather debts owed to him in strange currencies, and finally unbind the king at the gate itself — choosing justice outside the law over the order he served. The book ends with the crown shattered, the Veil passed willingly to Theo, and the child given a name and a home as the long winter breaks.
about_author: Sable Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing sealed estates and their stranger inheritances. They write fantasy about people who keep doors — and what comes through when the locks fail.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Theo Iversen balances the Veiled Guild's accounts: bottled storms, borrowed years, a widow's grief sold by the ounce. POV Theo. He is meticulous, lonely, and quietly proud of never asking where things come from. Emotional beat: comfortable routine established so it can be broken.

chapters.title: A Knock Before Dawn
chapters.summary: On the winter solstice eve, a small girl appears at the sealed gate, speaking a language no living tongue records — yet Theo understands it. She carries no shadow. POV Theo. Emotional beat: wonder laced with dread; his first instinct is to hide her, an act of rebellion he doesn't yet understand.

chapters.title: What the Masters Weigh
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane inspects the girl, calls her 'unregistered stock,' and orders her held for appraisal. Theo lies for the first time in twenty years of ledgers. POV Theo with a brief Corvane interlude. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Language Under Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Theo deciphers fragments of the girl's speech using forbidden folios; it is the tongue of the Veil itself, and she repeats one word like a name: the sleeping king's. POV Theo. Emotional beat: the thrill of scholarship curdling into responsibility.

chapters.title: Debts Owed in Strange Coin
chapters.summary: Theo calls in favors across the guild's black market: a ferryman paid in memories, a locksmith who owes him a death postponed. POV alternating Theo and the ferryman Odile. Emotional beat: discovering he is more loved than he believed.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: Corvane's appraisers measure the girl's value to 'a buyer in the capital' — the thing wearing King Aldric's crown. Theo learns the Guild built its fortune keeping the Veil thin enough to trade through. POV Odile, watching from the rafters. Emotional beat: righteous anger.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Frozen Market
chapters.summary: Odile creates a diversion among the stalls of impossible goods; Theo flees with the girl through collapsing ice-bridges above the market. POV Theo. Emotional beat: terror transformed into exhilaration — his first act of open defiance.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Was a Door
chapters.summary: Hiding in Odile's ferry-house, Theo learns the truth: the child isn't carrying the Veil, she IS it — made flesh when the old keepers died. She shows him visions of the crowned thing feeding on the king. POV the girl, rendered in her own perception. Emotional beat: tenderness and horror entwined.

chapters.title: Hunters of the Guild
chapters.summary: Corvane sends retrievers — debt-collectors whose contracts let them take years, names, or love. One finds them; Odile pays with a decade of her life to buy escape. POV Odile. Emotional beat: sacrifice, and Theo's guilt crystallizing into commitment.

chapters.title: The Road to the Capital
chapters.summary: The three travel north through villages where winter has stopped ending — fields frozen mid-harvest, hearths that won't light. The Veil is thinning everywhere. POV Theo. Emotional beat: mounting dread; the stakes become the whole world's warmth.

chapters.title: An Audience Refused
chapters.summary: In the capital they see King Aldric at a window procession: his eyes are wrong, moving a half-second behind his body. Courtiers wear veils against the cold that don't flutter. POV Theo. Emotional beat: the enemy revealed — patient, vast, wearing legitimacy.

chapters.title: The Loyal Shadow
chapters.summary: Captain Maren Voss, the king's sworn shield, catches Theo breaking into the palace archives — but she has suspected the king for months and buried the suspicion out of loyalty. POV Maren. Emotional beat: a lawkeeper confronting the limits of law.

chapters.title: Archives of the First Binding
chapters.summary: Maren leads them to sealed records: the Veil was forged by four keepers, and unbinding the king requires all four gates opened at once — including Theo's. The Guild was founded to prevent exactly this. POV Theo. Emotional beat: the trap of destiny; his gate is both key and cage.

chapters.title: Bargain with the Crowned Thing
chapters.summary: Corvane arrives in the capital and formally sells the girl's location to the court. Theo confronts him; Corvane offers Theo everything he ever wanted — mastery, belonging, the Guild itself. POV Theo. Emotional beat: temptation met and refused; the theme of belonging sharpened.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Guild retrievers seize the girl during a palace festival of lights. Theo is left bleeding in the snow, holding only her name — which she gave him freely, the one thing the Veil cannot be bought with. POV Theo. Emotional beat: despair at the darkest hour.

chapters.title: The Fourth Keeper
chapters.summary: Maren reveals the fourth gate lies beneath the palace itself, and the fourth keeper's line survives in her — she is descended from the king's first shield. Three keepers must now do the work of four. POV Maren. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance becoming true fellowship.

chapters.title: Storming the Winter Court
chapters.summary: During the longest night, Theo, Maren, and Odile infiltrate the throne room where the girl is bound before the crowned thing, being slowly unwoven. POV rotating among the three. Emotional beat: courage without any promise of survival.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: At the four gates — market, ferry, archive, throne — the keepers speak the girl's language together. The king wakes inside his own body for one lucid moment and begs release. Theo opens his gate last, choosing to break the order he served. POV Theo. Emotional beat: climax; justice enacted outside every law.

chapters.title: What Wears a Crown When It Falls
chapters.summary: The crowned thing, unbound from Aldric, reveals its true shape — the accumulated hunger of every bargain ever struck through the Veil. It offers Theo the world's warmth in exchange for the girl. He answers with her name, spoken as a refusal. POV the girl. Emotional beat: the power of naming against appetite.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Breaks
chapters.summary: The Veil collapses inward, taking the thing with it. Aldric dies human and free; thaw spreads from the palace outward. The Guild's ledgers burn in the frozen market as debts dissolve. POV Odile. Emotional beat: catharsis, grief for the king, relief like spring.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Open Gate
chapters.summary: The Veil settles into Theo, willingly accepted — he becomes its keeper not as a jailer but as a door held open on purpose. Corvane faces the guild's own reckoning; Maren rebuilds the court around a child heir. POV Theo. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined — what we choose to carry.

chapters.title: A Name and a Home
chapters.summary: Spring. Theo teaches the girl letters in two languages; she chooses her own name at last. The gate stands unlocked, tended but never again sealed, and travelers bring strange honest trades to a fairer market. POV the girl. Emotional beat: belonging earned, the arc complete.
